surge gdp-pdf

benchmark.surge.gdp-pdf

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Included after actual author, separate source-verifier and adversarial AI source-content reviews of exact approved bindings. Scope means the complete relevant available source documentation/methods actually recorded, with explicit bounded/unread pages, version differences and unknown rights, payload, construction or operations retained. No experiment, settled upstream rights, or human peer review is implied.

Review depth
full source
Disposition
included

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge gdp-pdf · human annotation: GDP.pdf’s v3 paper sources expert tasks from real work, rejects questions answerable from priors or ambiguous private context, and retains candidates only after at least two frontier models make a major meaningful error.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.gdp-pdf.curation.v2

  • Absolute pass rates therefore describe an adversarially selected set, not professional document work at large.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge gdp-pdf · evaluates: GDP.pdf’s v3 evaluation supplies each question and native PDF without tools, runs five trials per item and reports mean strict pass@1; Gemini 3.5 Flash judges each self-contained criterion without the PDF or reference answer.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.gdp-pdf.evaluation.v2

  • Mean criterion satisfaction is reported separately from all-criteria success; provider PDF processing is part of the measured configuration.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

surge gdp-pdf · human annotation: GDP.pdf’s paper describes expert-written atomic rubric criteria, including required abstention for unsupported queries, and sanity checks requiring the reference answer to pass and a deliberately bad output to fail the targeted criterion.

Permanent record ID: candidate.add17.gdp-pdf.rubric-checks.v2

  • Rubrics specify substantive facts and forbidden claims rather than relying on text-overlap similarity.
